key_insight: In tests using clinical trial reports with inserted methodological errors, LLMs detected more major errors than untrained human reviewers had in an earlier experiment.
clinical_relevance: LLM-assisted review could help identify methodological problems in clinical research, but false alarms require expert verification.
method: Tested 15 LLMs, including four open-weight models, on three trial reports with inserted errors.
Repeated testing on three trials published in 2026 to reduce memorization risk.
Evaluated control reports without inserted errors and measured review times.
evidence_signal: Major-error detection scores ranged from 53%–96% in the initial test and 51%–99% in the repeat test, versus 27% for untrained human reviewers in the earlier experiment.
watch_item: Models also flagged 2%–29% of error types in control reports, and performance on a small, deliberately altered report set may not generalize to routine peer review.
paper_title: Large language models detect methodological errors that human peer review misses in clinical trials
